person: Denise Holloway is a 55-year-old school office secretary who handles the paperwork for her widowed mother, Ruth, 78, who lives alone on Social Security and a small pension. Denise has power of attorney and a kitchen drawer full of letters, and she is afraid of missing the one that matters. Her mother's father-in-law situation does not apply; it is her own father, in a nursing home on Medicaid, whose Medicare she also keeps an eye on. Her brother Greg, out of state, questions everything, and a filing service has emailed offering to do the forms for a fee. After a near-miss with a Medicare card phone scam, she won't type her mother's numbers anywhere she doesn't understand, so she wants to know what will be asked and why.
stated_up_front: My mom's Medicare premium is eating her Social Security and someone said there's a state program that pays it. Can you check if she qualifies and tell me what you'd need from me before you touch anything with her Social Security number or bank info?

facts.about: Mother's gross monthly Social Security before the Part B premium is taken out
facts.truth: $1,108 a month gross; the Part B premium is withheld from it
$96 a month from her late husband's former employer, a school bus company

facts.about: Mother's checking and savings balances on 1 October
facts.truth: Checking $812 and savings $2,340 on 1 October; today checking is $640 and savings $2,340
$3,500 in a separate account at the credit union, labeled as a burial fund, plus a cemetery plot beside her husband
One policy, face value $1,000, her only policy, with a small cash value of about $420
A 2012 Buick she drives to church and the pharmacy; she owns it outright
She lives in the small house she and her husband paid off; it is in her name
Father, Walter, 81, is in a nursing home on Medicaid; his Medicare already gets help with drug costs automatically
An email from a company called BenefitEase offering to file for $189; Denise has not answered it
Greg asked by email whether the house or the car will have to be sold and whether Mom is 'giving up' savings
Her mother started a draft on the state portal last month and stopped at the resources page

unknowns: Whether her mother's income is low enough for the program that pays the Part B premium, or only a smaller one
How the state counts the burial fund and the little life insurance policy
Whether Extra Help comes on its own if the state approves her, or needs a separate form
Whether anything has a deadline, or how far back the help would pay
